To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nuclear shadowing in the structure functions measured at low x and moderate to high Q2 can be explained in the framework of the factorization approach and that the low Q 2 behavior of these observables and the measured large nuclear modification to the longitudinal structure function point towards a critical role of power corrections.

nuclear enhanced power corrections are important in the description of deeply inelastic lepton scattering on nuclei, and that the resummation of the perturbative expansion for these corrections is essential for a reliable quantitative description.

(1) The resummation of power corrections to F2A is necessary to explain the data at low x and Q2, (2) The resummations of the leading and subleading power corrections to the longitudinal structure function are required to describe its measured A dependence, (3) The subleading power corrections, which we calculate for the first time, are essential for the correct description of the data at low Bjorken x and Q2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear effects in the structure functions of the nucleon.
the calculation of the perturbative corrections to the leading twist approximation of nuclear deep inelastic scattering (DIS).
a perturbative calculation of the nuclear enhancement of the power suppressed terms of the Q2 expansion of F2A(x) and FAL(x), and with a resummation of the corresponding series.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resummation of nuclear enhanced power correction effects is a necessary step to make the QCD factorisation approach competitive with other theoretical models.

our resummation of the nuclear enhanced power corrections is in excellent agreement with the data, while the other theoretical approaches are in good agreement with the data at large Q2, but fail to describe the data at low Q2.
, while the power corrections are important, the present data do not allow us to determine them with precision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a new framework for understanding nuclear shadowing and that our results provide a new tool for the analysis of future data from the HERA and Jefferson Lab.
the QCD factorized approach, which includes the power corrections, can describe the nuclear data in the whole kinematic range of the available data.
nuclear enhanced power corrections are important for understanding the data and for a quantitative understanding of shadowing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power corrections are not a perturbative series in 1/Q, but rather a series in 1/lnQ.
power corrections are not only necessary but also calculable in the QCD factorisation approach.

the resummed power corrections can explain the data at low Q2 without invoking a new mechanism for nuclear shadowing, and thus provide a consistent description of nuclear structure functions at all Q2.
